_comment: What the Brokild Collection zip is supposed to contain, declared rather than inferred.
A collection is a DERIVED artefact: it goes stale the moment the fleet gains or
renames a plugin, and it had done so twice before anyone noticed. So every plugin
that ships a -VST3-win64.zip must appear in exactly one of the two lists below,
and tools/check-links.js fails if it does not, or if the archive on disk disagrees
with 'includes', or if the site's wording contradicts the count.
Adding a plugin to the fleet therefore forces a decision about the collection
instead of leaving one to be remembered. Re-cutting the zip is a Windows job -

excludes.hairfryer: In development - its own card says so, and a collection billed as finished work should not carry it.
excludes.rite-of-passage: Left out on purpose: its zip carries the .vst3 bundle and a GUIDE.md, with no standalone and no manual, so it does not have the shape the other entries do - every plugin in the archive gets a folder with a bundle, an application and a handbook. Peter also asked for it to be kept minimal ("you can just store it in the VST3 folder"). Give it a standalone and a manual and it belongs here.
excludes.legion: Same reason as rite-of-passage: VST3 only, no standalone and no manual yet.

pending.1984: INTO the Brokild Collection. A finished instrument with a standalone, an 18-page handbook, 40 patches and a bench of 87 checks; it was simply never placed.
_comment: DECIDED, not yet cut. A plug-in here is agreed to move and will do so at the
next re-cut of the collections; until then `includes` goes on describing what
the archive on disk really holds. check-links.js accepts a plug-in in exactly
one of includes, excludes or pending, and refuses one that appears in two.
The three collections were agreed on 2026-09-23. See REPO-CONSOLIDATION.md.
pending.rite-of-passage: INTO the Brokild Collection, once it has a standalone and a manual. It ships a bundle and a GUIDE.md today, and every folder in that archive holds a bundle, an application and a handbook.
pending.thirty-thousand-years: INTO the Brokild Collection, once it is finished. Another session is still building it.
pending.hairfryer: Moves from excluded INTO the Experimental Collection, where a plug-in that is still in development belongs.
pending.legion: INTO the Experimental Collection, once it has a landing page of its own so it is findable outside the archive.

claims._comment: Repeated across app.json, the collection page and the front page. Checked so a re-cut cannot update the zip and leave the prose saying ten. While `pending` is non-empty this describes the CURRENT archive, not the agreed one.

download._comment: The archive is a GitHub RELEASE ASSET, not a file in this repository. At eleven plugins it is 101 MB and GitHub refuses any file over 100 MB outright - the push is rejected, so there is no choice to make. Git LFS is not an option either: GitHub Pages serves an LFS pointer rather than the file. Re-cutting therefore means uploading a new asset and pointing this url at it. The zip is kept on the PC beside this file, untracked, which is why the archive check in tools/check-links.js still runs there and skips in CI.
